honesty.banner: Sample / demo dataset — not a live relationship graph. Cascades are illustrative educational patterns, not current-event forecasts.
honesty.confidenceRules: Observed is reserved for established structural facts. Predicted or downstream hops must never use Observed. Missing or invalid confidence defaults to Unknown.
honesty.evidenceRules: Demo evidence uses example.invalid citations and historical pattern notes. Never treat these as live news.

relationships.why: A large share of advanced chip fabrication capacity is concentrated in Taiwan — a structural fact used for literacy, not a prediction.

evidence.label: Illustrative industry concentration note (demo)
evidence.notes: Demo citation. Replace with verified public sources before live mode.

relationships.why: Electronics assembly depends on steady semiconductor supply for boards and controllers.

evidence.label: Illustrative supply-input pattern (demo)
evidence.notes: Historical pattern, not a live shortage claim.

relationships.why: Modern vehicles embed electronics for powertrain, safety, and infotainment — chip and board delays can constrain builds.
Vehicle availability and pricing feed into what households can purchase and when.

evidence.label: Illustrative consumer availability hop (demo)
evidence.notes: Citizen-impact literacy; not a price forecast.

relationships.why: When a major gateway slows, scheduled container capacity through that corridor tightens.

evidence.label: Illustrative port throughput pattern (demo)
evidence.notes: Demo only — not a live port status.

relationships.why: Missed vessel windows cascade into warehouse and trucking schedules inland.
Retail restock calendars depend on predictable inbound logistics.
Households may notice thinner shelves or longer waits when retail inbound slows — not overnight shocks.

evidence.label: Illustrative citizen-impact hop (demo)
evidence.notes: Low confidence by design for distant citizen effects.

relationships.why: A tariff on imported steel can raise effective input cost for domestic buyers of that steel.

evidence.label: Illustrative tariff price-pass pattern (demo)
evidence.notes: Mechanism literacy; not a claim about any current measure.

relationships.why: Construction projects budget steel as a major structural input; cost shifts can delay or reprice builds.
Vehicle body and chassis manufacturing consumes steel; input cost and availability matter for production planning.
Prolonged drought can reduce yields or raise irrigation stress for grain-producing regions.
Food processors buy grain as a core feedstock for flour, feed, and packaged foods.
Processing cost and availability can eventually show up in grocery prices — usually with lag and many other factors.
Conflict near energy corridors can raise risk premiums and disrupt tanker schedules for crude shipments.

evidence.label: Illustrative corridor-risk pattern (demo)
evidence.notes: Educational; not a live conflict report.

relationships.why: Crude price and availability feed refined fuel costs that transportation operators pay.
Higher transport costs can reprice freight contracts and slow discretionary shipments.
Export-control rules can limit which advanced chips may be shipped to certain destinations without licenses.

evidence.label: Illustrative export-control mechanism (demo)
evidence.notes: Policy literacy; not a live license advisory.

relationships.why: Device makers that rely on advanced nodes may redesign, delay, or substitute when licensed supply tightens.
OEM delays can lengthen wait times or change specs for consumer and enterprise devices.
A fab company produces semiconductors that later industries consume — company → commodity literacy.

evidence.label: Illustrative fictional fab (demo)
evidence.notes: Fictional company. Never present as a real issuer.

relationships.why: A constrained canal corridor reduces daily transit capacity for container schedules that rely on that shortcut.

evidence.label: Illustrative canal capacity pattern (demo)
evidence.notes: Aligned with Articles sample canal brief; still demo-labeled.

relationships.why: Longer ocean legs and missed slots delay imported finished goods.
Retail assortments that depend on imports face restock risk when inbound goods slip.

When transportation fuel and schedule costs rise, passenger travel — including airlines sensitive to jet-fuel and network delays — can see fare and reliability pressure. This is a structural literacy hop, not a live fare claim.

evidence.label: Illustrative travel cost sensitivity (demo)
evidence.notes: Provenance: explain-this seed extension aligning Relationship Explorer with Citizen Impact gsn_travel. Low confidence by design.
